title: Cap. X: Theologorum auxilium — Whitaker, Chamier, Sixtus, Bellarmine
pass_a_gloss: With that reason thus set out, Garissoles joins to himself the help of the theologians and names Whitaker (Vitakerus), Chamier, Sixtus of Siena, and Bellarmine. That he praises our men is no surprise: so it is customary in this cause, to drive off the suspicion of novelty. But why the Papists? Why Bellarmine? Did he think we could be moved by their authority? Placeus thinks not: rather he wanted to join Bellarmine's reasons to his own to attack Placeus's side. For he says Bellarmine comes forward propped by reasons not to be despised for confirming this opinion, in book 5 On the Loss of Grace and the State of Sin, chapter 18. Come then, let us also dissolve his reasons — and with the more courage because, if Placeus understands anything, they are not obscurely adverse to the doctrine of original sin received in our churches.
pass_b_english: With that argument laid out, Garissoles calls in the theologians' help and names Whitaker, Chamier, Sixtus of Siena, and Bellarmine. That he praises our writers does not surprise me: that is how this debate usually goes when novelty is the charge to be shaken off. But why the Papists? Why Bellarmine? Did he think their authority would move us? I do not think so. He meant to join Bellarmine's reasons to his own against us. He says Bellarmine comes forward on no contemptible grounds for confirming this opinion — book 5 of On the Loss of Grace and the State of Sin, chapter 18. Very well: let us answer those reasons too, and with the more spirit because, if I understand them, they cut plainly against the doctrine of original sin received in our churches.
source_text: Hac ratione sic proposita Theologorum auxilium sibi adjungit, & Vitakerum, Chamierum, Sixtum Senensem, & Bellarminum nominat. Nostros cur laudet non miror: ita enim in hac causa usuvenit, novitatis suspicionem amoliendi causa: Sed cur Pontificios? cur Bellarminum? Nosne putavit eorum autoritate moveri posse? Non arbitror: Sed suis rationibus conjungere voluit ad nos oppugnandos Bellarmini rationes. Eum enim dicit non contemnendis ad firmandam hanc sententiam rationibus fultum procedere in medium lib. 5. de Amiss. Grat. & Stat. pecc. cap. 18. Age igitur hujus etiam solvamus rationes, eoque majore animo quod si quid intelligo, receptae in Ecclesiis nostris doctrinae de peccato originali non obscure adversantur.

choices.decision: not for papal authority but to add his rationes to Garissoles's attack; Placeus answers because they clash with Reformed original-sin doctrine
